violated_assumptions: Candidate assumes duplicate collection creation should return an error, but Milvus contract specifies idempotent behavior when schema is unchanged
The oracle appears to expect an error on ANY duplicate, but the documented behavior distinguishes between same-schema (200) vs different-schema (error 65535) cases

contract_refs: constraint_id: milvus_state_collections_create_001 - 'collection creation is atomic AND collectionName is unique within dbName; re-creating an existing collection with the SAME schema is an idempotent no-op returning 200'
constraint_id: milvus_behavioral_collections_create_002 - 'duplicate collection name with the same schema returns 200 (idempotent no-op), with a different schema returns an error'
invariant_id: milvus_invariant_create_duplicate_001 - 'create(collection, schema A) -> create(collection, schema A) returns 200 (idempotent no-op)'

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: CreateCollectionRequest -> validateIfCollectionExists -> GetCollectionByName -> Equal check -> return errIgnoredCreateCollection if schemas match
source_grounding.note: Source code explicitly implements idempotent duplicate collection creation: when collection exists with SAME schema (Equal check passes), it returns errIgnoredCreateCollection, which is caught in root_coord.go line 903-907 and converted to HTTP 200 success. This is intentional by-design behavior, not a bug.

verdicts.rationale: Milvus explicitly specifies and implements idempotent collection creation: re-creating a collection with the SAME schema returns HTTP 200 (no-op success), while re-creating with DIFFERENT parameters returns error 65535. The candidate expects an error on duplicate creation regardless of schema, which contradicts both the documented contract (milvus_state_collections_create_001, milvus_behavioral_collections_create_002, milvus_invariant_create_duplicate_001) and the verified source implementation (create_collection_task.go:522-540, root_coord.go:903-907). Source code shows errIgnoredCreateCollection is returned when schemas match and explicitly converted to success response. This is by-design idempotent behavior, not a defect.
